s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with chest pain and ECG changes in a patient with a history of coronary artery bypass surgery
salient_findings: Dull chest pain of 2 hours' duration
ST segment depression >1mm in V2 and V3
New discordant ST elevation of 1mm in leads II, III, and aVF
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
History of coronary artery bypass surgery
Ejection fraction of 25%
Biventricular pacemaker placement
Chest pain duration of 2 hours
ECG shows sinus activity at 72 beats/min
QRS duration of 160 milliseconds
Ventricular depolarization preceded by 2 pacing stimuli
Initial troponin was negative
Cardiac catheterization revealed thrombotic occlusion of saphenous vein graft
Occlusive lesions in proximal obtuse marginal artery

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of coronary artery bypass surgery and cardiac catheterization revealed thrombotic occlusion of the saphenous vein graft, which explains the chest pain and ECG changes.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Initial troponin was negative, which makes acute myocardial infarction less likely

rejected.label: Unstable angina
rejected.why: While possible, the presence of thrombotic occlusion of the saphenous vein graft makes graft occlusion a more specific diagnosis

rejected.label: Native coronary artery disease
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and catheterization results are more consistent with a problem related to the graft rather than native coronary artery disease

rejected.label: Prinzmetal's angina
rejected.why: There is no evidence of transient ST segment elevation in multiple leads, which is characteristic of Prinzmetal's angina
